english: Let $a$ be a real number and let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function such that $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}f(t)\,dt=x^{3}+ax^{2}$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. The region bounded by the curve $y=f(x)$ and the $x$-axis lies in the fourth quadrant and has area $4$. If $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is defined by $g(x)=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}f(t)\,dt$, then the least value of $g$ on $[0,\infty)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$ एक वास्तविक संख्या है तथा $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक ऐसा सतत फलन है कि सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}f(t)\,dt=x^{3}+ax^{2}$ है। वक्र $y=f(x)$ तथा $x$-अक्ष द्वारा परिबद्ध क्षेत्र चतुर्थ चतुर्थांश में स्थित है तथा उसका क्षेत्रफल $4$ है। यदि $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}f(t)\,dt$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, तो $[0,\infty)$ पर $g$ का न्यूनतम मान ______ है।
solution: The region is in the fourth quadrant, so it lies over $x>0$ and below the axis: $-\dfrac{2a}{3}>0\Rightarrow a<0$, with $f<0$ on $\left(0,-\dfrac{2a}{3}\right)$.
$g'(x)=f(x)$: $g$ decreases on $[0,2]$, increases on $[2,\infty)$; least value $g(2)=8-12=-4$ (equal to minus the area, since $g(2)$ is the signed area from $0$ to $2$).
solution_full: $f$ is continuous, so by the first part of the fundamental theorem, $\dfrac{d}{dx}\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}f(t)dt=f(x)$. Differentiating the identity gives $f(x)=3x^{2}+2ax=x(3x+2a)$.
$a\ne 0$, otherwise $f=3x^{2}\ge 0$ touches the axis only at $0$ and bounds no region. The zeros are $x=0$ and $x=-\dfrac{2a}{3}$, and $f<0$ strictly between them (upward parabola).

So the bounded region lies below the $x$-axis between the two zeros. It is in the fourth quadrant iff these $x$ are positive, i.e. $-\dfrac{2a}{3}>0$, $a<0$. (For $a>0$ it would lie in the third quadrant.)

By the second part of the theorem, $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{b}f(t)dt=g(b)-g(0)=b^{3}+ab^{2}$. With $b=-\dfrac{2a}{3}$: $\int_{0}^{b}f=b^{2}(b+a)=\dfrac{4a^{2}}{9}\cdot\dfrac{a}{3}=\dfrac{4a^{3}}{27}$, which is negative.

On $[0,\infty)$: $g'(x)=f(x)<0$ on $(0,2)$ and $>0$ on $(2,\infty)$, so the least value is $g(2)=8-12=-4$. It equals minus the area, because $g(2)$ is the signed integral of $f$ over exactly the region below the axis.
originality_note: New: the accumulation function g of f is minimised exactly at the end of the region under the axis, so the least value of g equals minus the given area (way 4, hidden link between the signed integral and the area). Closest known: find f from an integral identity and then an area. Different because: the quadrant condition fixes the sign of a and the final answer reads the area back through g.

concept_use.Area bounded by a curve and the x-axis;: The region lies below the axis on (0, -2a/3), so the area is minus the signed integral, -4a^3/27 = 4.
concept_use.Fundamental theorem of calculus (both pa: First part: differentiating gives f = 3x^2 + 2ax and g' = f for the minimum; second part: the integral of f over [0,b] equals g(b) - g(0).

stem_review: Read as a student: every function introduced with its domain, every condition stated, one reading, answer unique and equal to the plan; Hindi mirrors the English maths. Checked a = 0 gives no region and a > 0 gives the third quadrant, so a = -3 is forced; restricted the minimum to [0, infinity) because g is unbounded below on R. No further change.
key_step: Use the quadrant to fix the sign of a, then recognise g(2) as the signed area.
justification: Two linked ideas (FTC to recover f and to read g' = f, sign handling of the area) with a sign trap; numerical. Close to 2024-P2-Q13 (L3), which also reads zeros of an integral function.
